## Make a simple regression model

```{r}
bears <- read.csv(file="BEARS.csv",header = TRUE)
#adjust factors to be factors
bears$SEX<- as.factor(bears$SEX)
bears$MONTH<- as.factor(bears$MONTH)
```

## Model LENGTH ~ NECK  this is an example  

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ NECK,data=bears)
```


As neck diameter increases Length tends to also increase. The plot is primarily linear. 


```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH~NECK,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```

 The adjusted R-squared is 0.7476.  

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADLEN

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears)
```

As the head length increases, the length of the bear also increases. 

```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```

The adjusted R-squared is 0.8463, bigger than the previous models.
